proof_scope: regression cases for defects observed in live operation, run against the real CLI and the real routing library with an isolated state root

claims.proves: each named failure mode is refused or handled as described, repeatably, through the skill's own entrypoint and routing functions; that the installed cron interval is never every-minute, that dispatch defers during the overnight batch window, and that activate reports schedule and state together
claims.does_not_prove: that a live repair, closure audit, or completion attestation succeeds. Those dispatch models through $ask/Tau and are proven only by a live receipt read back from the produced artifact, not by this fixture.

cases.name: closure-audit-nonzero-needs-attention
cases.proves: A closure audit whose Ask/Tau wrapper exits nonzero but whose seats declare VERDICT: NEEDS_ATTENTION is not sent down the no-verdict path; it attempts durable closure-unverified handling and records cooldown state so the next tick does not re-launch the duplicate audit.
cases.does_not_prove: A live browser/provider closure audit succeeds; this is a fault-injected regression over the watchdog's own handler and cooldown path.

cases.name: dirty-registered-target-does-not-block-isolated-authoring
command: repo=$(git -C .. rev-parse --show-toplevel) && cd "$repo" && uv run --project skills/project-watchdog pytest skills/project-watchdog/tests/test_project_watchdog.py::test_a_dirty_registered_target_is_reported_but_does_not_block_isolated_authoring skills/project-watchdog/tests/test_project_rotation.py::test_dirty_target_is_reported_without_blocking_isolated_dispatch -q
cases.proves: Dirty tracked files in the registered checkout are reported but do not block issue selection or isolated repair authoring.
cases.does_not_prove: A live Ask/Tau repair for the ticket succeeds.

cases.name: overlapping-applied-ticks-skip-live
command:
cd ..; D=$(mktemp -d); printf '%s
' '{"schema":"agent_skills.project_watchdog.registry.v1","projects":[]}' > $D/projects.json; printf '%s
' '{"global":{"state":"active"},"projects":{}}' > $D/state.json; PROJECT_WATCHDOG_STATE_ROOT=$D PROJECT_WATCHDOG_PROJECTS_PATH=$D/projects.json PROJECT_WATCHDOG_TEST_HOLD_LOCK_SECONDS=8 ./run.sh tick --apply --project all --max-tickets 1 > $D/first.out 2> $D/first.err & first=$!; for i in $(seq 1 80); do [ -f $D/lock/owner.json ] && break; sleep 0.1; done; test -f $D/lock/owner.json || { echo FIRST_LOCK_NOT_OBSERVED; cat $D/first.err; kill $first 2>/dev/null || true; wait $first 2>/dev/null || true; exit 1; }; python3 - <<PY
import json, pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('$D/lock/owner.json')
d=json.loads(p.read_text())
d['epoch']=0
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2)+'\n')
print('FIRST_RUN='+d['run_id'])
PY
PROJECT_WATCHDOG_STATE_ROOT=$D PROJECT_WATCHDOG_PROJECTS_PATH=$D/projects.json ./run.sh tick --apply --project all --max-tickets 1 > $D/second.out 2> $D/second.err; second_rc=$?; wait $first; first_rc=$?; python3 - <<PY
import json, pathlib, sys
root=pathlib.Path('$D')
second_rc=int('$second_rc')
first_rc=int('$first_rc')
second=json.loads((root/'second.out').read_text())
assert second_rc == 0, (second_rc, (root/'second.err').read_text())
assert second['status']=='SKIPPED', second
assert second['stop_reason']=='tick_already_running', second
assert second.get('handled_issues') == [], second.get('handled_issues')
assert second.get('receipt_persisted') is False, second
assert first_rc == 0, (first_rc, (root/'first.err').read_text())
print('OVERLAP_SKIPPED_LIVE')
PY
